episode.title: The Battle of the Windmill
episode.context: On Animal Farm, the animals have overthrown their human masters and now live under the rule of the pigs, led by Napoleon. They've been working tirelessly to build a windmill that promises to make their lives easier, while Napoleon consolidates his power through propaganda, fear, and manipulation.
episode.art_style: Watercolor storybook illustration with earthy pastoral tones, visible brushstrokes, soft golden lighting reminiscent of classic children's book illustrations
episode.narrator_style: warm, deliberate storyteller with gentle irony

clover.name: Clover
clover.description: A stout motherly mare approaching middle age, with a kind face and worried eyes. Her gray coat shows the wear of hard work, and she moves with the careful gait of an animal who has seen much and remembers more than she can express.

benjamin.name: Benjamin
benjamin.description: An old donkey with a gray coat showing patches of white from age. His expression is perpetually cynical, and he moves slowly and deliberately. He is the oldest animal on the farm and rarely shows emotion.

napoleon.name: Napoleon
napoleon.description: A large, fierce-looking Berkshire boar with a commanding presence. His eyes are small and calculating, and he carries himself with an air of absolute authority. He wears two medals pinned to his chest and is often accompanied by a retinue of fierce dogs.

squealer.name: Squealer
squealer.description: A small fat pig with round cheeks, twinkling eyes, and a shrill voice. His movements are quick and nimble, and he has a way of skipping from side to side when making a persuasive argument, his tail whisking persuasively.

farmhouse.name: The Farmhouse
farmhouse.description: A comfortable two-story dwelling with white walls, now somewhat yellowed. It has a proper kitchen, a drawing room with furniture, and bedrooms with real beds. Once occupied by the human farmer Jones, it stands apart from the humble barns where the other animals sleep.

barn_wall.name: The Barn Wall
barn_wall.description: The great wall of the big barn where the Seven Commandments were once painted in large white letters. The paint is now faded and weathered, and the wall itself looks different from how it used to.

windmill.name: The Windmill
windmill.description: A half-constructed stone tower rising from a hill on the farm. Built from rough-hewn limestone blocks hauled from the quarry, its walls grow slowly but steadily. It represents both the animals' hopes for a better future and the crushing weight of their endless labor.

snowball.name: Snowball
snowball.description: A young, energetic pig with round cheeks and quick, intelligent eyes. His white and brown spotted coat is always clean, and he carries himself with the confident posture of a natural leader and thinker.

boxer.name: Boxer
boxer.description: An enormous draft horse with a white stripe down his nose and tremendously powerful muscles. His coat is a deep chestnut brown, worn and dusty from constant labor. Despite his size, his eyes are gentle and trusting, though increasingly tired. He wears a simple rope harness frayed from overuse.

mollie.name: Mollie
mollie.description: A foolish, pretty white mare with a flowing mane she takes great pride in. She wears ribbons when she can get them and has a vain, flirtatious manner. Her coat is always carefully groomed.

mr_jones.name: Mr. Jones
mr_jones.description: A disheveled middle-aged farmer with a red face and unkempt hair. Wears a worn tweed jacket and carries a double-barreled shotgun. His expression is bitter and resentful.

manor_farm.name: Manor Farm
manor_farm.description: A traditional English farm with a large red barn, stone farmhouse with a thatched roof, rolling green pastures, an orchard, and a pond. Hedgerows line the fields, and a five-barred wooden gate marks the entrance from the main road.

the_barn.name: The Great Barn
the_barn.description: A large, weathered red barn with a high peaked roof. Its wooden walls show years of use, but it stands strong and proud at the heart of the farm, now serving as the animals' meeting hall.

the_farmhouse.name: The Farmhouse
the_farmhouse.description: A two-story white farmhouse with green shutters, now abandoned by humans. A flagpole stands in the garden, and the harness-room has been converted into the pigs' headquarters.

animal_farm.name: Animal Farm
animal_farm.description: A working English farm with a red barn, stone farmhouse, and green pastures surrounded by wooden fences. A green flag with a white hoof and horn flies from a flagpole in the yard.

the_dogs.name: Napoleon's Dogs
the_dogs.description: Nine enormous, fierce dogs with brass-studded collars. They are wolf-like in appearance with sharp teeth and menacing eyes, always staying close to Napoleon.

windmill_site.name: The Windmill Knoll
windmill_site.description: A small grassy hill, the highest point on the farm, overlooking the pastures and farm buildings. The wind blows steadily across its top, making it an ideal spot for a windmill.

quarry.name: The Quarry
quarry.description: A limestone quarry on the edge of the farm, littered with massive boulders. A steep slope leads to its top, worn smooth by countless hooves dragging stones upward. The ground is scarred with rope marks and the desperate scraping of hooves.

barn.name: The Big Barn
barn.description: A large wooden barn with peeling red paint where the animals gather for meetings. On its end wall, the Seven Commandments are painted in white letters, though the paint seems to change mysteriously over time.

van.name: The Knacker's Van
van.description: A large enclosed van drawn by two horses, with sinister lettering on its side reading 'Alfred Simmonds, Horse Slaughterer and Glue Boiler, Willingdon.'

sentences: In the days following the terrible executions on Animal Farm, a quiet unease settled over the animals.
Some of them remembered, or thought they remembered, that one of their sacred commandments said no animal shall kill another animal.
But when Clover asked to have the commandment read to her, it turned out to say something different than she recalled.
scenes.video_description: A somber morning on Animal Farm, mist rising from the fields. Animals stand in small groups, their heads bowed, speaking in hushed tones. The big barn looms in the background with its painted commandments barely visible through the fog.
scenes.camera_style: Wide establishing shot, slowly drifting across the farmyard

sentences: The commandment now read: No animal shall kill any other animal without cause.
Those last two words, 'without cause,' had somehow slipped out of everyone's memory.
But seeing them there now, the animals convinced themselves the rule had never been broken after all.
scenes.video_description: Close-up of the barn wall where the Sixth Commandment is painted in white letters. The words 'WITHOUT CAUSE' appear slightly fresher than the rest, the paint subtly different. A sheep stares up at it, blinking in confusion.
scenes.camera_style: Slow push-in on the commandment, focusing on the added words

sentences: Throughout that year, the animals worked harder than ever before.
They had to rebuild the windmill with walls twice as thick, while still managing all the regular work of the farm.
Sometimes it felt like they worked longer hours and ate less than they had back in the old days under Farmer Jones.
scenes.video_description: Animals laboring in the fields under a hot sun. Horses pull heavy carts of stone, sheep carry smaller loads, and chickens scratch at the hard ground. Their bodies show signs of exhaustion, ribs visible beneath their coats.
scenes.camera_style: Sweeping shot across the working animals, emphasizing their toil

sentences: Every Sunday morning, Squealer would read them impressive lists of numbers.
Food production was up two hundred percent here, three hundred percent there, five hundred percent somewhere else.
The animals couldn't quite remember what life had been like before, so they had no way to argue with the figures.
Though privately, many wished they could have fewer statistics and more actual food.
scenes.video_description: Squealer stands on a raised platform, holding a long scroll of paper covered in numbers. The assembled animals look up at him with tired, trusting eyes. Their food troughs in the background appear nearly empty.
scenes.camera_style: Medium shot of Squealer, then panning across the listening animals

sentences: Napoleon had become a rare sight on the farm, appearing perhaps once every two weeks.
When he did emerge, it was quite a spectacle.
He walked surrounded by his fierce guard dogs, with a black rooster marching ahead of him, crowing loudly to announce his arrival.
scenes.video_description: Napoleon emerges from the farmhouse in a grand procession. Nine large dogs flank him on either side, and a proud black cockerel struts before him. The other animals press back respectfully, clearing a wide path.
scenes.camera_style: Low angle shot emphasizing Napoleon's imposing presence

sentences: Inside the farmhouse, Napoleon had taken over the best rooms for himself.
He ate his meals alone from the finest china, with two dogs standing by to serve him.
The gun was now fired on his birthday, and he was spoken of only with elaborate titles.
Our Leader Comrade Napoleon, they called him, Father of All Animals, Protector of the Sheep-fold.
scenes.video_description: Interior of the farmhouse dining room, Napoleon seated alone at a grand table. Fine china gleams before him, and two attentive dogs stand at his shoulders. Through the window, the other animals can be seen working in the fields.
scenes.camera_style: Slow dolly shot through the dining room, contrasting luxury with the view outside

sentences: The pigs invented all sorts of ways to praise Napoleon.
A hen might say that under his guidance, she had laid five eggs in six days.
Cows drinking from the pond would exclaim how excellent the water tasted, thanks to his leadership.
A pig named Minimus even composed a poem in Napoleon's honor, which was painted on the barn wall alongside his portrait.
scenes.video_description: Various scenes of animals praising Napoleon: a hen proudly showing eggs, cows at a pond raising their heads in gratitude. Then the barn wall where a crude portrait of Napoleon in profile appears next to a painted poem.
scenes.camera_style: Quick cuts between praising animals, ending on the barn wall portrait

sentences: Meanwhile, Napoleon was conducting secret business through a human middleman named Whymper.
The farm had a valuable pile of timber to sell, and two neighboring farmers, Frederick and Pilkington, both wanted it.
Frederick owned a tough, efficiently run farm called Pinchfield, while Pilkington's Foxwood was larger but more neglected.
Terrible rumors circulated about Frederick, how he starved his animals and committed unspeakable cruelties.
scenes.video_description: A dark office scene where Whymper, a shrewd-looking man in a worn suit, examines documents by lamplight. Through the window, the silhouettes of two neighboring farms are visible in the distance, one neat and menacing, the other sprawling and wild.
scenes.camera_style: Intimate interior shot with dramatic shadows

sentences: Napoleon announced publicly that he would never deal with Frederick, that scoundrel.
The pigeons were sent out with a new slogan: Death to Frederick.
Official word came that Napoleon was becoming friends with Pilkington instead.
The animals felt relieved, Pilkington seemed like the lesser evil.
scenes.video_description: Pigeons fly out from the barn in formation, carrying banners with anti-Frederick slogans. Below, animals nod approvingly while Napoleon watches from the farmhouse porch with apparent satisfaction.
scenes.camera_style: Following shot tracking the pigeons against a cloudy sky

sentences: Rumors continued to swirl about the exiled pig Snowball, who had been blamed for everything that went wrong on the farm.
When weeds appeared in the wheat, Squealer explained that Snowball had snuck in at night and mixed weed seeds with the corn.
The animals also learned that Snowball had never actually been a hero in the great battle years ago.
In fact, he had shown cowardice and had been censured, not decorated.
scenes.video_description: A dreamy, distorted vision of Snowball as a shadowy, villainous figure sneaking through wheat fields at night, scattering seeds of destruction. The image wavers like a bad memory, unreliable and sinister.
scenes.camera_style: Surreal, wavering focus suggesting propaganda and false memory

sentences: Some animals felt confused by this, they thought they remembered things differently.
But Squealer was always there to help them understand that their memories were simply at fault.
And somehow, they always ended up believing him.
scenes.video_description: Clover and Benjamin stand together, looking troubled. Squealer approaches with his persuasive manner, gesturing and explaining. Clover's expression slowly shifts from doubt to reluctant acceptance.
scenes.camera_style: Close-up on the animals' faces, capturing their internal struggle

sentences: Finally, in autumn, the windmill was finished.
Through exhaustion and sacrifice, working through the harvest, the animals completed their masterpiece.
The walls stood twice as thick as before, strong enough to withstand almost anything.
Tired but proud, the animals gathered to admire what they had built.
scenes.video_description: The completed windmill stands tall against an autumn sunset, its stone walls golden in the fading light. Animals gather around it in a circle, some leaning against each other in exhaustion, all gazing up with wonder and pride.
scenes.camera_style: Majestic wide shot, slowly circling the windmill

sentences: Napoleon himself came down to inspect the work, accompanied by his dogs and his crowing rooster.
He congratulated the animals on their achievement and announced that the mill would be named Napoleon Mill.
The animals cheered, their weariness forgotten in the moment of triumph.
scenes.video_description: Napoleon struts around the base of the windmill, nodding approvingly. The animals cheer and stamp their hooves. A sign reading 'NAPOLEON MILL' is unveiled, and the dogs bark in celebration.
scenes.camera_style: Dynamic shot capturing the celebration atmosphere

sentences: Two days later, Napoleon called a special meeting that left everyone speechless.
He announced that he had sold the timber, not to Pilkington as everyone expected, but to Frederick.
All that talk of friendship with Pilkington had been a clever trick to drive up Frederick's price.
The pigeons were immediately sent out with a new slogan: Death to Pilkington.
scenes.video_description: Inside the crowded barn, animals stand in stunned silence as Napoleon makes his announcement. Their expressions shift from shock to confusion to reluctant acceptance. Pigeons flutter out through the doors with new orders.
scenes.camera_style: Reaction shots of various animals, then following the departing pigeons

sentences: Squealer praised Napoleon's brilliant cunning.
Not only had he gotten a better price, but he had demanded payment in real cash, not a check.
Frederick paid in crisp five-pound notes, enough to buy the machinery for the windmill.
Napoleon displayed the money proudly in a special meeting, letting each animal file past to admire it.
scenes.video_description: Napoleon reclines on a bed of straw, medals gleaming, with stacks of banknotes arranged on a china dish beside him. Animals pass by one at a time, gazing at the money with awe. Boxer extends his nose to sniff the notes curiously.
scenes.camera_style: Slow procession shot, lingering on the gleaming money

sentences: Three days later, everything fell apart.
Whymper came racing up the path on his bicycle, his face white as a sheet.
Moments later, a roar of rage echoed from Napoleon's private rooms.
The terrible news spread across the farm like wildfire: the banknotes were forgeries.
scenes.video_description: Whymper's bicycle crashes into the farmyard as he leaps off and runs toward the house. Through a window, Napoleon's silhouette is seen in a rage. Animals cluster together, passing the news in horrified whispers.
scenes.camera_style: Fast-paced sequence building tension, ending on terrified animals

sentences: Frederick had cheated them completely, getting all that timber for nothing.
Napoleon pronounced a death sentence on Frederick, declaring he should be boiled alive when captured.
But there was no time for revenge.
The very next morning, Frederick and fifteen armed men attacked Animal Farm.
scenes.video_description: Dawn breaks over Animal Farm with an ominous red sky. On the horizon, a line of men with guns advances through the morning mist. Animals race frantically across the farmyard, sounding the alarm.
scenes.camera_style: Wide shot of the approaching threat, then cutting to panicked animals

sentences: The animals charged out bravely to meet the invaders, but this battle was nothing like their easy victory years ago.
The men had guns and knew how to use them.
Pellets tore through the air, and the animals were forced to retreat to the farm buildings.
They hid and watched through cracks in the walls as the enemy took control of the pasture.
scenes.video_description: Chaos of battle: animals charging forward, then scattering as gunfire erupts. Boxer rears up heroically while other animals flee to the barn. Smoke and dust fill the air as the men advance steadily.
scenes.camera_style: Intense action sequence with quick cuts between fighting and fleeing

sentences: Even Napoleon seemed at a loss, pacing back and forth with his tail twitching nervously.
Some animals looked hopefully toward Pilkington's farm, wondering if help might come.
But the pigeons they had sent returned with a bitter message scrawled on paper.
It read simply: Serves you right.
scenes.video_description: Napoleon paces anxiously while animals peer out from hiding. A pigeon lands with a small piece of paper. An animal reads it, and the hope drains from their faces. In the distance, Pilkington's farm sits quiet and unhelpful.
scenes.camera_style: Tense close-ups of worried faces, then the devastating message

sentences: Then the animals saw something that made their blood run cold.
Two of Frederick's men were working at the base of the windmill with a crowbar and hammer.
Napoleon insisted the walls were too thick to knock down.
But old Benjamin, watching carefully, understood exactly what they were doing.
scenes.video_description: Through a crack in the barn wall, animals watch as two men drill at the windmill's foundation. Benjamin's knowing eyes narrow. The other animals look confused, but Benjamin's expression is one of grim understanding.
scenes.camera_style: POV shot through barn crack, then close-up on Benjamin's face

sentences: They're packing blasting powder into that hole, Benjamin said quietly.
The animals watched in helpless horror as the men ran away from the windmill.
Then came a deafening explosion that shook the very earth.
When the smoke cleared, the windmill had ceased to exist.
scenes.video_description: The men retreat rapidly. A moment of terrible silence, then an enormous explosion. The windmill erupts in a cloud of black smoke and flying stones. Animals throw themselves flat, covering their faces. When they look up, only rubble remains.
scenes.camera_style: Slow motion explosion, then devastated aftermath

sentences: Something changed in the animals at that moment.
Their fear and despair transformed into pure, burning rage.
Without waiting for orders, they charged at the enemy.
They no longer cared about the guns or the pellets that swept over them like hail.
scenes.video_description: The animals' expressions shift from horror to fury. As one, they surge forward from the buildings, a wave of desperate courage. Gunfire flashes but they keep coming, united in their anger.
scenes.camera_style: Dramatic charge sequence, low angle emphasizing the animals' determination

sentences: It was a savage, bitter battle.
Boxer's mighty hooves cracked the heads of three men.
A cow gored another with her horns.
When Napoleon's dogs appeared suddenly from behind, flanking the enemy, panic overtook the humans.
scenes.video_description: Close combat between animals and men. Boxer rears up magnificently, striking down attackers. Dogs appear from the hedgerow, snarling and baying. The men's confidence breaks as they find themselves surrounded.
scenes.camera_style: Intense battle montage with focus on key moments of animal triumph

sentences: Frederick shouted for his men to retreat while they still could.
The cowardly enemy ran for their lives, with the animals chasing them to the edge of the farm.
They got in some last kicks as the men forced their way through the thorn hedge.
The battle was over, Animal Farm had won.
scenes.video_description: Men scramble and flee across the fields, animals pursuing. Frederick runs at the front of his retreating forces. The animals stop at the farm boundary, chests heaving with exhaustion but heads held high in victory.
scenes.camera_style: Triumphant tracking shot of the enemy's retreat

sentences: But victory had come at a terrible cost.
The animals limped back toward the farm, weary and bleeding.
A cow, three sheep, and two geese lay dead on the field.
Nearly every survivor carried wounds, and some paused to weep at the sight of their fallen comrades.
scenes.video_description: The aftermath of battle: wounded animals helping each other across the torn-up field. Bodies of the fallen lie peacefully in the grass. Surviving animals pause to mourn, some leaning against each other for support.
scenes.camera_style: Somber tracking shot across the battlefield

sentences: And then they came to where the windmill had stood.
The explosion had been so powerful that the stones had been flung hundreds of yards in every direction.
Even the foundations were destroyed.
Two years of backbreaking labor had vanished in a single moment, as if the windmill had never existed at all.
scenes.video_description: Animals gather at a crater where the windmill once stood. Scattered stones lie across the fields. Boxer stares at the destruction, his great shoulders slumped. The setting sun casts long shadows across the devastation.
scenes.camera_style: Slow, mournful pan across the ruins

sentences: Just then, Squealer came bouncing toward them, somehow having missed the entire battle.
His tail whisked with satisfaction as he announced that the gun was being fired to celebrate their victory.
Victory? Boxer asked, blood dripping from his wounds, pellets lodged in his leg.
They destroyed our windmill, and we worked on it for two years.
scenes.video_description: Squealer approaches the exhausted, wounded animals with an incongruous cheerfulness. In the background, smoke rises from the farmhouse gun. Boxer looks at Squealer with genuine confusion, his injuries clearly visible.
scenes.camera_style: Contrasting shots between cheerful Squealer and wounded Boxer

sentences: What does that matter? Squealer exclaimed, we will build another windmill, we will build six windmills if we feel like it.
The enemy occupied our sacred soil, and thanks to Napoleon's leadership, we have won every inch of it back.
Boxer considered this slowly, his tired mind working through the logic.
Then we have won back what we had before, he said at last.
scenes.video_description: Squealer gestures grandly while explaining the 'victory.' Boxer's face shows the struggle to understand. Other animals listen, too tired to question. The destroyed windmill site looms behind them all.
scenes.camera_style: Two-shot dialogue between Squealer and Boxer

sentences: That is our victory, Squealer declared triumphantly.
For the first time, Boxer felt the full weight of his eleven years.
He looked at the rubble and imagined the immense labor of rebuilding from nothing.
Perhaps his great muscles were not quite what they had once been.
scenes.video_description: Boxer stands alone, gazing at the rubble. His posture shows weariness and age. The other animals disperse in the background. A close-up reveals the gray in his muzzle, the wear in his eyes.
scenes.camera_style: Intimate character study of Boxer's exhaustion

sentences: But then the green flag went up over the farmhouse, and the gun fired again, seven times in all.
Napoleon gave a speech congratulating them, and somehow it did start to feel like a victory.
The fallen animals were given a solemn funeral, with Napoleon himself leading the procession.
There were songs and celebrations, special gifts of apples and corn, and a new medal that Napoleon awarded to himself.
scenes.video_description: A grand ceremony unfolds: the green flag waves, guns boom, Napoleon speaks from a platform. A funeral procession passes solemnly. Then celebrations begin with food being distributed. Napoleon pins a medal to his own chest.
scenes.camera_style: Montage of ceremony and celebration, mixing triumph with mourning

sentences: The battle would be remembered as the Battle of the Windmill.
In all the celebrations, the unfortunate matter of the forged banknotes was completely forgotten.
After all, they had won, hadn't they?
That was what Napoleon told them, and Napoleon was never wrong.
scenes.video_description: Animals feast on their special rations, their wounds bandaged. The forged banknotes lie crumpled and forgotten in a corner of the farmhouse. Napoleon watches over the celebration with cold, satisfied eyes.
scenes.camera_style: Wide shot of celebration, then subtle focus on the forgotten evidence of deception

sentences: A few days later, the pigs made an interesting discovery in the farmhouse cellar.
A case of whisky had been overlooked when the animals first took over.
That night, strange sounds came from the farmhouse, loud singing mixed with the old forbidden anthem, Beasts of England.
Someone even spotted Napoleon wearing Mr. Jones's old bowler hat, galloping drunkenly around the yard.
scenes.video_description: Night scene: warm light glows from the farmhouse windows. Muffled singing echoes across the dark farmyard. A comical silhouette of Napoleon in a bowler hat careens past a window. Other animals watch from their stalls in bewilderment.
scenes.camera_style: Atmospheric night shots with comedic glimpses of pig revelry

sentences: The next morning, a terrible silence hung over the farmhouse.
Not a pig stirred until nearly nine o'clock, when Squealer finally emerged.
He walked slowly, eyes dull, tail hanging limp, looking desperately ill.
He gathered the animals and told them he had terrible news: Comrade Napoleon was dying.
scenes.video_description: A gray, quiet morning. Squealer emerges from the farmhouse looking genuinely unwell, moving with none of his usual energy. Animals gather anxiously as he delivers his grave announcement. Some begin to weep.
scenes.camera_style: Subdued lighting and slow movements conveying crisis

sentences: A cry of grief went up across the farm.
Straw was laid outside the farmhouse doors, and the animals walked on tiptoe.
With tears in their eyes, they wondered what they would do without their Leader.
As his final act, Napoleon issued a solemn decree: from this day forward, the drinking of alcohol would be punished by death.
scenes.video_description: Animals gather in mourning outside the farmhouse, many weeping openly. They lay straw carefully at the threshold. Through a window, Napoleon is glimpsed lying in apparent agony. A new decree is posted on the barn.
scenes.camera_style: Emotional scenes of collective grief and anxiety

sentences: But by evening, Napoleon seemed somewhat better.
By the next day, he was well on the way to recovery.
And shortly after that, he sent Whymper into town to purchase booklets on brewing and distilling.
The retirement pasture that had been promised to old animals was quietly plowed up to grow barley instead.
scenes.video_description: Napoleon up and about, looking recovered if slightly sheepish. Whymper rides off with a shopping list. In the background, the small pasture is being plowed. A faded sign reading 'Retirement Pasture' is tossed aside.
scenes.camera_style: Sequence showing Napoleon's recovery and its ironic consequences

sentences: One night around midnight, a loud crash woke the animals.
They rushed out to find Squealer lying stunned at the foot of the barn wall.
Beside him lay a ladder, a lantern, a paintbrush, and an overturned pot of white paint.
The dogs quickly escorted him away, and no one could figure out what had happened.
scenes.video_description: Moonlit farmyard scene. Animals emerge from their stalls to find Squealer sprawled beneath the painted commandments. Evidence of his night's work lies scattered around him. Dogs hustle him away before questions can be asked.
scenes.camera_style: Mystery-style reveal of the incriminating scene

sentences: Only old Benjamin seemed to understand, nodding his gray muzzle with a knowing look.
But as always, Benjamin refused to explain.
He had seen too much in his long life to be surprised anymore.
scenes.video_description: Benjamin stands apart from the confused crowd, his expression one of weary understanding. He turns away from the scene without comment. His eyes hold decades of witnessed betrayals.
scenes.camera_style: Character-focused shot on Benjamin's knowing face

sentences: A few days later, Muriel happened to read the Fifth Commandment to herself.
She could have sworn it said no animal shall drink alcohol.
But looking at it now, she saw there were two words she must have forgotten.
The commandment actually read: No animal shall drink alcohol to excess.
scenes.video_description: Muriel the goat stands before the barn wall, squinting at the painted words. The addition 'TO EXCESS' is visible in slightly fresher paint. She shakes her head, doubting her own memory, and walks away troubled.
scenes.camera_style: Close-up on the altered commandment, then Muriel's confused face

sentences: And so life continued on Animal Farm.
The commandments kept changing, but somehow the animals always seemed to have remembered them wrong.
The pigs grew fatter while everyone else worked harder.
And if any animal dared to question, well, Squealer was always there to help them understand.
scenes.video_description: A montage of farm life: animals laboring while pigs supervise from comfortable positions. The barn wall with its commandments, paint dripping ominously. Squealer explaining something to a group of bewildered sheep. Life goes on under Napoleon's watchful eye.
scenes.camera_style: Sweeping summary shots of daily life on the farm

sentences: As for the windmill, they would have to build it again.
They always would.
And somehow, no matter how hard they worked, things never quite got better.
But that was just how it was on Animal Farm, where all animals were equal, but some animals were more equal than others.
scenes.video_description: Final wide shot of the farm at sunset. The crater where the windmill stood dominates the landscape. Animals trudge wearily to their quarters while pigs retire to the comfortable farmhouse. The green flag hangs limp in the still air.
scenes.camera_style: Slow pull-back to wide establishing shot, fading to dusk
